site.course.ada.intro: Ada is made for software that must not fail, from aircraft to railways. You learn strong typing, decisions, loops, procedures and functions, arrays, your own types and records.
site.course.ada.tagline: Safe and reliable – for planes, trains and space.
site.course.assembly.intro: Assembly is the human-readable form of machine instructions. In x86-64 assembly for Linux you learn registers, system calls, arithmetic, comparisons and jumps, loops, memory, the stack and functions.
site.course.assembly.tagline: Talk to the CPU – registers, memory and jumps.
site.course.bash.intro: Bash is the shell of Linux and macOS and the glue of automation. You learn scripts, variables, arguments, decisions, loops, functions, pipes and text tools, and arrays.
site.course.bash.tagline: Automate your computer from the command line.
site.course.c.intro: C is the language behind operating systems, databases and countless devices. You learn printf, variables and types, operators, decisions, loops, functions, arrays and strings, pointers and structs.
site.course.c.tagline: The classic – how computers really work.
site.course.clojure.intro: Clojure is a modern Lisp on the JVM with immutable data at its heart. You learn prefix notation, values, functions, decisions, collections, sequences, recursion and working with maps.
site.course.clojure.tagline: A modern Lisp – simple, functional, immutable.
site.course.cobol.intro: COBOL still runs a large part of the world's banking and insurance business. You learn the divisions of a program, data with PIC clauses, arithmetic, decisions, loops with PERFORM, paragraphs, tables and text handling.
site.course.cobol.tagline: The language behind banks and insurers.
site.course.common-lisp.intro: Common Lisp is one of the oldest and most flexible languages – code and data look the same. You learn s-expressions, values, functions, decisions, lists, higher-order functions, loops and recursion, and data structures.
site.course.cpp.intro: C++ powers games, browsers, engines and embedded systems. You learn variables, decisions, loops, functions, vectors, strings, classes, references and pointers.
site.course.cpp.tagline: Powerful and fast – for games, engines and systems.
site.course.crystal.intro: Crystal looks like Ruby but compiles to fast native code with static types. You learn variables and types, strings, decisions, loops, methods, arrays and hashes, and classes.
site.course.csharp.intro: C# is the main language of .NET for desktop apps, web services and games with Unity. You learn variables, strings, decisions, loops, methods, collections and classes.
site.course.csharp.tagline: Modern and versatile – apps, games and the web with .NET.
site.course.d.intro: D combines the power of C and C++ with modern features like ranges and automatic memory management. You learn variables and types, strings, decisions, loops, functions, arrays and structs.
site.course.d.tagline: The power of C with modern comfort.
site.course.dart.intro: Dart is the language of Flutter, used to build apps for phones, the web and desktops from one code base. You learn variables and null safety, strings, decisions, loops, functions, collections and classes.
site.course.dart.tagline: One language for apps on every screen.
site.course.delphi.intro: Delphi is Object Pascal, known for building native apps quickly. You learn console programs, variables and types, strings, decisions, loops, procedures and functions, arrays and classes.
site.course.delphi.tagline: Object Pascal for fast native apps.
site.course.elixir.intro: Elixir is a friendly functional language on the Erlang VM, made for scalable, fault-tolerant systems. You learn basic types, pattern matching, decisions, functions and pipes, lists and maps, Enum and recursion.
site.course.elixir.tagline: Functional and fault-tolerant – built for the web.
site.course.erlang.intro: Erlang powers telecom systems and chat apps that must never stop. You learn values and pattern matching, functions with clauses and guards, lists, recursion, maps and lightweight processes.
site.course.erlang.tagline: Built for systems that never go down.
site.course.fortran.intro: Fortran has powered scientific computing for decades and still runs on supercomputers today. You learn variables and types, arithmetic and formatted output, decisions, loops, arrays, functions and subroutines, and derived types.
site.course.fortran.tagline: The language of science and supercomputers.
site.course.fsharp.intro: F# is a concise, functional-first language on .NET. You learn values and types, functions and pipes, decisions and match, lists, recursion, records and unions, and options.
site.course.gleam.intro: Gleam is a friendly, type-safe functional language that runs on the Erlang VM and on JavaScript. You learn values and types, strings, functions and pipes, pattern matching, lists, recursion and custom types.
site.course.gleam.tagline: Friendly and type-safe on Erlang and JavaScript.
site.course.go.intro: Go is a simple, fast language from Google for servers, command-line tools and cloud software. You learn variables, control flow, functions, slices, maps, structs, interfaces and error handling.
site.course.go.tagline: Simple and fast – made for servers and the cloud.
site.course.haskell.intro: Haskell is a purely functional language with a powerful type system. You learn values and types, functions, guards and case, lists, map and filter, recursion with pattern matching and your own data types.
site.course.java.intro: Java runs on billions of devices, from Android apps to large business systems. You learn classes and main, variables and types, strings, decisions, loops, methods, arrays and lists, classes and records.
site.course.java.tagline: Runs everywhere – from Android to big business.
site.course.javascript.intro: JavaScript makes websites interactive and also runs on servers with Node.js. You learn variables, operators, decisions, loops, functions, arrays and objects.
site.course.javascript.tagline: The language of the web – runs in every browser.
site.course.julia.intro: Julia is a fast, high-level language for science, numbers and data. You learn variables and types, strings, decisions, loops, functions and multiple dispatch, arrays, dictionaries and structs.
site.course.julia.tagline: Fast and friendly – made for science.
site.course.kotlin.intro: Kotlin is concise, safe and the preferred language for Android apps; it also runs on servers. You learn variables, strings, decisions, ranges, functions, collections, classes and null safety.
site.course.kotlin.tagline: Concise and safe – the modern language for Android.
site.course.lua.intro: Lua is a tiny, fast scripting language used in games like Roblox and in many apps. You learn print, variables and types, strings, decisions, loops, functions, and tables as lists, dictionaries and objects.
site.course.lua.tagline: Small, fast and built into games.
site.course.machine-code.intro: Under every program are bytes that the CPU executes. You learn binary and hexadecimal, how numbers are stored, how x86-64 instructions are encoded, jumps and offsets, and you read a whole program byte by byte.
site.course.machine-code.tagline: Bits, bytes and opcodes – how the CPU sees programs.
site.course.nim.intro: Nim reads like Python but compiles to fast native code. You learn echo, variables and types, strings, decisions, loops, procedures, arrays and sequences, and objects.
site.course.nim.tagline: Reads like Python, runs like C.
site.course.objective-c.intro: Objective-C is C with objects and messages – the classic language of macOS and iOS. You learn Foundation, variables and types, NSString, decisions, loops, arrays and dictionaries, classes and properties.
site.course.objective-c.tagline: The classic language of Apple platforms.
site.course.ocaml.intro: OCaml is a functional language with strong static types, used for compilers, finance and tools. You learn values and types, functions, decisions and match, lists, recursion, variants and records, and options.
site.course.ocaml.tagline: Functional with strong types – safe and fast.
site.course.odin.intro: Odin is a modern systems language with a simple syntax, popular for games and graphics tools. You learn variables and types, decisions, loops, procedures, arrays and slices, structs and enums, and maps.
site.course.odin.tagline: A simple systems language for games and tools.
site.course.pascal.intro: Pascal was designed to teach clear, structured programming and lives on in Free Pascal and Lazarus. You learn variables and types, operators, decisions, loops, procedures and functions, arrays and strings, and records.
site.course.pascal.tagline: Structured and clear – a classic for learning.
site.course.perl.intro: Perl is a powerful scripting language, famous for working with text. You learn scalars, decisions, loops, arrays, hashes, subroutines and regular expressions.
site.course.perl.tagline: The Swiss army knife of text processing.
site.course.php.intro: PHP powers a large part of the web, from WordPress to Laravel. You learn echo, variables and types, strings, decisions, loops, functions, arrays and classes.
site.course.php.tagline: The language behind much of the web.
site.course.prolog.intro: In Prolog you describe facts and rules, and the computer finds the answers. You learn facts and queries, rules, unification, arithmetic, recursion, lists and collecting solutions.
site.course.prolog.tagline: Logic programming – describe what is true.
site.course.python.intro: Python is easy to read and used everywhere: for automation, data analysis, AI and the web. You learn print, variables, strings, decisions, loops, lists, dictionaries and functions.
site.course.python.tagline: Easy to read – the language of AI and data.
site.course.r.intro: R is the language of statistics, data analysis and charts in science. You learn variables and types, vectors, decisions, loops, functions, lists and apply, and data frames.
site.course.r.tagline: The language of statistics and data analysis.
site.course.racket.intro: Racket is a modern Lisp, popular in teaching and for creating new languages. You learn values, functions, decisions, lists, higher-order functions, recursion and loops, and structs.
site.course.racket.tagline: A Lisp for learning and building languages.
site.course.ruby.intro: Ruby is an elegant language known for Ruby on Rails and readable code. You learn puts, variables and types, strings, decisions, loops and ranges, methods, arrays and hashes, and classes.
site.course.ruby.tagline: Elegant and friendly – made for happy programmers.
site.course.rust.intro: Rust is a fast, memory-safe language for tools, servers and systems. You start with your first program and learn variables, ownership, borrowing, structs, enums, traits and iterators.
site.course.rust.tagline: Fast and safe – from println! to traits.
site.course.scala.intro: Scala combines object-oriented and functional programming and runs on the JVM. You learn values and types, strings, decisions and match, loops and ranges, functions, collections and case classes.
site.course.scala.tagline: Object-oriented meets functional on the JVM.
site.course.scheme.intro: Scheme is a small, elegant Lisp, famous for teaching the core ideas of programming. You learn values, procedures, decisions, lists, recursion, higher-order procedures, strings and vectors.
site.course.scheme.tagline: Minimal and elegant – the Lisp of teaching.
site.course.smalltalk.intro: Smalltalk shaped object-oriented programming: everything is an object, and work happens through messages. You learn messages, variables, decisions and blocks, loops, collections and classes.
site.course.smalltalk.tagline: Everything is an object – the original OOP.
site.course.solidity.intro: Solidity is the language of smart contracts on Ethereum and other blockchains. You learn contracts, types and state, functions, require, loops and arrays, mappings and structs, events and errors, and a tiny token.
site.course.sql.intro: SQL is how you read and change data in databases – in almost every company and app. You learn queries, filtering, sorting, functions, aggregates, grouping, joins and how to change tables.
site.course.sql.tagline: The language of databases – ask your data questions.
site.course.swift.intro: Swift is Apple's modern language for apps on iPhone, iPad and Mac. You learn constants and variables, strings, decisions, loops, functions, closures, collections, optionals and structs.
site.course.swift.tagline: Clean and fast – apps for iPhone, iPad and Mac.
site.course.typescript.intro: TypeScript adds types to JavaScript, so many mistakes show up before your code runs. You learn basic types, functions, interfaces, union types, arrays, classes and generics.
site.course.typescript.tagline: JavaScript with types – catch mistakes early.
site.course.v.intro: V is a small language with a simple syntax, safety by default and very fast compilation. You learn variables and types, strings, decisions and match, loops, functions, arrays and maps, structs and options.
site.course.v.tagline: Simple, fast and safe – compiles in a blink.
site.course.zig.intro: Zig is a small, modern systems language without hidden control flow – a fresh alternative to C. You learn printing, variables and types, decisions, loops, functions, arrays and slices, structs, and error handling with optionals.
site.course.zig.tagline: Simple and precise – a modern C alternative.

site.privacy_contact_text: Responsible: Nico Rene Zweers – see the legal notice.
site.privacy_intro: nrzLearn works without an account and without cookies. Here is what happens with your data:
site.privacy_local_text: Progress (levels, stars, XP, streak) and settings (language, course, dark mode, daily goal, sounds) are stored only in your browser's local storage (localStorage). They are not sent to our server. You can export, import or delete them at any time on the profile page; clearing your browser data deletes them as well.
site.privacy_local_title: Your progress stays in your browser
site.privacy_meta_description: How nrzLearn handles your data: no account, no cookies, no advertising – your progress stays in your browser.
site.privacy_none_text: There is no registration and no login. nrzLearn sets no cookies and uses no advertising services. The server delivers the files of the app (HTML, JavaScript, WebAssembly, CSS and the course texts) and receives only the anonymous counts described below.
site.privacy_playground_text: Only when you run a code example or a code exercise in the Rust course, your browser sends that code to the official Rust Playground (play.rust-lang.org), run by the Rust project, where it is compiled and executed. The Playground's own privacy terms apply to that. The other courses do not send any code.
site.privacy_playground_title: Running code in the Rust course: Rust Playground
site.privacy_stats_text: When you finish a level, your browser sends an anonymous count to our server: which course, which interface language and which kind of level. It contains no ID, no cookie and nothing that identifies you, and the server does not store your IP address with it. We only use the totals, for example to see which courses are popular.
